The evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered left zygomatic maxillary comminuted fracture and left orbital blow out fracture and there is also evidence to indicate that the claimant was treated as inpatient at various hospital for a period of 12 days.
The dental surgeon was examined as P.W.3, who assessed disability to the whole body at 20% and the Tribunal has accordingly assessed the disability at 7%.
In my view, assessment of disability cannot be found fault with.

3. The Tribunal despite noticing that the claimant was aged about 18 years has decided to apply the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd and Ors - AIR 2014 SC 736 and awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards permanent disability.

entities.text: Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd and Ors - AIR 2014 SC 736
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In my view, this assessment would be incorrect and multiplier method would have been adopted, as the claimant was aged about 18 years and the accident occurred in the year 2016.

A sum of Rs.9,500/- is taken as notional income as per the determination by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority and accordingly, the claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.1,43,640/- (9500 x 12 x 18 x 7%) towards loss of future income.

4. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering and Rs.20,000/-
towards loss of future amenities.

Having regard to the fact that the claimant has suffered multiple fractures and is in hospital for a period of 12 days, it is appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/-
towards pain and suffering and Rs.75,000/- towards loss of future amenities.
5. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.13,000/- towards attendant charges, in my view, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.20,000/-.
6. The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as two months.

In my view, having regard to the multiple fractures, it would be appropriate to take three months and the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.28,500/- towards loss of income during the laid up period.
7.
A sum of Rs.1,62,217/- towards medical expenses and Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses is correct.

8. The evidence on record also indicates that there has been a certain degree of facial disability due to injuries suffered by the claimant towards his face and having regard to the fact that the claimant was aged about 18 years, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards marriage prospects.
9.

Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.5,74,357/- as against Rs.3,93,217/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
11. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
12. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
